paper.title_en: Gravitational lensing and deflection angles of generalised Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole embedded in a warped braneworld background
paper.abstract_en: We investigate null geodesics, deflection angles, and gravitational lensing by the generalized Ellis-Bronnikov (GEB) wormhole and its embedding in a five-dimensional warped braneworld (WGEB). The GEB geometry extends the standard Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a steepness parameter $m\geq 2$, which controls the throat profile while partially reducing the violation of the classical energy conditions. We derive analytic expressions for the weak- and strong-deflection angles and obtain the corresponding Einstein-ring and relativistic-image relations. The standard Ellis-Bronnikov results are recovered as the special case $m=2$, while for $m>2$ the strong-deflection angle exhibits a power-law divergence instead of the familiar logarithmic behaviour. For the warped five-dimensional geometry, we show that the extra-dimensional momentum modifies the effective impact parameter, and hence the deflection angle and image positions while leaving the location of the unstable photon orbit unchanged. We further derive generalized relations between relativistic and non-relativistic Einstein-ring radii. Our analysis shows that deflection/ring data alone cannot distinguish the effect of the warped extra dimension in WGEB scenario.
